                "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 24 at 4:04PM MDT until October 26 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Southwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...\nEastern Kane County in southern Utah...\n\n* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Monday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding along the San Juan River is occurring.\nLow-water crossing will be inundated with water and may not be\npassable. The river is running fast and high. Do not attempt to\ncross.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 352 PM MDT, the San Juan River is forecast to continue to rise\nand crest near midnight Sunday night at Bluff.  Flooding will\ncontinue downstream to the terminus at Lake Powell through Monday\nmorning.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nThe San Juan River from downstream of Bluff to the terminus at\nLake Powell.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",

In the Farmington vicinity,\nbackwater flooding on the Animas River at and above the confluence\nwith the San Juan River is the major concern. See flood bulletins\npertaining to the Animas River.                 "description": "* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.\n\n* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast beaches of\nPuerto Rico and Culebra.\n\n* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away\nfrom shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to\nreturn to safety.",
                "instruction": "There is a high risk of rip currents.\n\nRip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away\nfrom shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the\nsandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties\nand piers.                 "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,\nnortheast, and southeast New Mexico, including the following areas,\nin central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County,\nEstancia Valley, Middle Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque\nMetro Area, Sandia and Manzano Mountains including Edgewood, South\nCentral Highlands and South Central Mountains. In east central New\nMexico, De Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New\nMexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley,\nFar Northwest Highlands, Glorieta Mesa Including Glorieta Pass,\nJemez Mountains, Northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Northwest\nHighlands, Santa Fe Metro Area, Southern Sangre de Cristo\nMountains, Tusas Mountains Including Chama and Upper Rio Grande\nValley. In northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far\nNortheast Highlands, Johnson and Bartlett Mesas Including Raton\nPass and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves\nCounty Plains and Southwest Chaves County.\n\n* WHEN...Through late tonight.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be\nflooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Showers and thunderstorms will expand in coverage though the\nafternoon. Rainfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour may cause\nflash flooding on already saturated soils. Arroyos, small streams\nand channels may quickly rise with water from heavy rainfall.\nRepeated rounds of storms will increase the risk for flash\nflooding.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "description": "* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of\ninundation above ground level in low-lying areas near\nshorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Rip Current Risk,\ndangerous rip currents. Low-lying roads and\nlocations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal\ncreeks may observe minor coastal flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best\nswimmers away from shore into deeper water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on\naverage tide conditions. Additional locations may experience\nflooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or\nother factors.",
                "instruction": "If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be\nclosed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of\nunknown depth.                 "headline": "Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:15AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nSt Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.\n\n.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns\nat Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage.                 "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU",
                "description": "30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall\nIslands at 700 AM ChST this morning, located near 10.6N 166.3E, or\n120 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of Bikini and Rongelap\nAtolls. In-fa has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph, which extend\noutward 115 miles to the southeast, 105 miles to the southwest, 100\nmiles to the northwest, and 40 miles to the northeast. This keeps\nUjae Atoll just outside the direct tropical storm-force wind field,\nbut strong sustained west to southwest winds with damaging tropical\nstorm-force gusts are expected through at least tonight as In-fa\nbegins to meander generally northward. The worst impacts will be\nfelt for islands and atolls across the northern and central Marshall\nIslands, especially for west-facing exposures along the Ralik Chain,\nsuch as Ujae, Enewetak, and Kwajalein Atolls. To the south of In-fa,\nexpect surging west to southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts\nup to 45 knots, especially near heavier showers or outflow\nboundaries. Boats should be safely secured away from west or south-\nfacing exposures, if possible. Significant boat damage has been\nreported along west reefs already.\n\nSeas will be hazardous to small craft throughout much of the central\nand northern RMI, and dangerous within the tropical storm-force\nwinds closer to the center of In-fa. Do not attempt inter-island\ntravel. Even within the relatively calmer lagoon-side waters, inter-\nisland travel is strongly discouraged. Passing showers may produce\nsudden strong to gale-force gusts, which will create locally\ndangerous conditions. West to southwest swells will build to the\nsouth of In- fa through the rest of the weekend, leading to elevated,\npotentially hazardous surf along west- and south-facing reefs of the\ncentral and northern RMI, mainly to the north and northwest of\nMajuro.\n\nCurrently, In-fa is nearly-stationary, with its recent motion showing\na slight southeastward drift at around 1 mph, but is forecast to\nbegin slowly meandering north-northeast, then north-northwest through\nthis afternoon. Then, In-fa will see a slight increase in forward\nspeed through Sunday as it begins to exit the Marshall Islands. Winds\nand seas will begin to ease through Sunday night, but sea conditions\nmay remain hazardous to small craft across the northern Marshalls\nthrough Monday night. Light winds and a drier ridging pattern look to\nset up across the region by the end of the week. This situation\nwill be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall\nIslands.\n\nFor more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to\nbulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header\nWTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header\nWTPQ31 PGUM.",
